title: Lobster Bisque
subtitle: Classic French cream soup of lobster and brandy
excerpt: A rich, velvety French cream soup made from lobster shells, vegetables, and brandy, finished with a swirl of cream. Deeply luxurious and far better homemade than from a tin.

recipe.sourceNotes: Bisque is a smooth, rich French cream soup made from crustaceans (lobster, crab, prawn, or crayfish) and characterised by a cooking method in which the shells are roasted, then simmered with vegetables and wine to extract every drop of flavour before the soup is strained, blended, and finished with cream. The word bisque may derive from Biscay (the Bay of Biscay) or from the French bis cuites (twice cooked), referring to the roasting of the shells before simmering. The technique of roasting the shells in butter or oil is fundamental: the Maillard reactions and caramelisation of the shell create the deep, complex flavour that distinguishes a proper bisque from a simple cream soup. Lobster bisque can be made using the shells from cooked lobsters after the meat has been eaten, making it an excellent way to use what might otherwise be discarded.

recipeTools.notes: A large, heavy saucepan. A blender. A fine sieve.

content.text: Roasting the lobster shells in oil before simmering them is the key step: it deepens the flavour dramatically compared to simply simmering raw shells. Crush the shells slightly before roasting to expose more surface area. The brandy is added after roasting and ignited (flambéed) to burn off the alcohol and add flavour; take care when doing this. Strain the bisque through a fine sieve and press hard on the shells and vegetables to extract all the liquid before blending. The cream is stirred in at the end; do not boil after adding it.

items.preparation: shells from 2 cooked lobsters, crushed; or 2 uncooked lobster tails

content.text: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over high heat. Add the crushed lobster shells and roast, stirring, for 5 minutes until they turn red and begin to char slightly at the edges. Add the onion, carrot, celery, and garlic. Cook for 3 minutes.

Add the tomato puree and cook for 1 minute. Add the brandy and allow it to bubble for 30 seconds. Add the wine, tinned tomatoes, stock, thyme, and bay. Season with salt and cayenne. Simmer for 35 to 40 minutes.

Strain through a fine sieve, pressing hard on the shells. Transfer the strained liquid to a blender and blend until smooth. Return to the pan and stir in the cream. Heat gently without boiling. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve with a swirl of cream and crusty bread.
